values.AssociatedLNGNotes: A Boardwalk Pipelines press release from October 2025 says the Texas Gateway Project is meant to supply Texas gas to LNG exporters, utilities, and industrial users near Gillis, Louisiana. An Oil and Gas Journal article from July 2026 says it would serve demand from LNG export plants along the Louisiana Gulf Coast. No source names one terminal.

verifications.note: Names the Texas Gateway Project and says it is designed to give LNG exporters access to Texas gas and supports the next wave of LNG growth.
Says the project would connect East Texas gas with demand from LNG export plants on the Louisiana Gulf Coast.

records.researcher_notes: Two sources tie the project to LNG exporters in general. Neither names a single terminal, so the terminal cell is left blank.

values.AssociatedLNGNotes: Tellurian planned this pipeline to bring Haynesville gas to Southwest Louisiana alongside its Driftwood LNG export project. A Natural Gas Intelligence article from August 2020 says Tellurian deferred it while advancing Driftwood. Driftwood is now the Woodside Louisiana LNG terminal.

verifications.note: Names the Haynesville Global Access Pipeline and says it was deferred as Tellurian worked toward a decision on the Driftwood LNG export terminal.
Names the pipeline and describes it as incremental to the Driftwood LNG export project near Lake Charles.
